title: Pakistan Calls Israel's Refusal to Withdraw from Gaza a 'Serious Setback'
detail: Pakistan publicly condemned Israel's refusal to withdraw forces from Gaza, describing it as a 'serious setback' to peace efforts. Islamabad's statement adds a prominent Muslim-world diplomatic voice to growing international pressure on stalled ceasefire negotiations, signaling broader solidarity against Israel's continued military presence.

media.caption: Pakistan condemns Israel's refusal to withdraw from Gaza as a serious setback to peace

title: Hamas Denounces Israel for Killing Top Gaza Police Official in Targeted Strike
detail: Hamas condemned Israel for carrying out a targeted strike that killed a senior Gaza police official. The killing drew sharp condemnation from Hamas, which accused Israel of deliberately targeting civil security personnel. The strike underscores continued Israeli operations against Hamas-affiliated security and administrative figures in Gaza. Al Jazeera identified the victim as Colonel Jamal Abu Kamil, 43, head of the civil police force in Gaza City: an Israeli drone fired three missiles at his vehicle on Al-Rashid Street southwest of Gaza City, killing him and wounding two others. The IDF claimed he posed "a threat" and alleged he was a Hamas commander, without providing evidence; Gaza's police force denied this, saying Abu Kamil "committed to his police duties and has no connection to other activities." Gaza's Ministry of Interior called the killing an "assassination." The same day, a separate Israeli strike in Khan Younis killed one person and critically wounded another.

media.caption: Hamas denounces Israel for killing a top Gaza police official in targeted strike

title: IDF Disciplines Five Soldiers Over Photographed Abuse of Bound Gaza Detainee
detail: The Israeli military said on August 13, 2026 that it had disciplined five soldiers after an internal investigation into an incident in which a Palestinian detainee from Gaza was stripped, restrained to a bed with his hands tied behind his back, blindfolded, and photographed. One soldier posted the image to Instagram with the caption "Good morning." The IDF said the detainee had been restrained after attempting self-harm, but concluded the manner in which he was treated, photographed, and had his image circulated online violated military values. Punishments included military prison sentences (two soldiers received five days each), removal from combat duty, base restrictions, and position transfers. Human rights organizations said such documented abuse of detainees could constitute a war crime under international law.

media.caption: IDF disciplines five soldiers over the photographed abuse of a bound Palestinian detainee from Gaza
